scope.description: In-process single-voter Cluster: bootstrap a configuration entry, become leader, apply five commands, then restart the node on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore with a fresh transport. Three cases: restore_committed_logs on with no snapshot; off with no snapshot; on with a snapshot taken before the restart. Observations are the node's configuration size (GetConfiguration), whether it reaches Leader again, applied/commit indices, and staged commit index at restart.
assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs is a documented public Config field (config.go 243-254) that is enabled by the application; the probe only supplies that documented configuration.
The existing test TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs always snapshots before restarting (raft_test.go 1183-1280), so the configuration-in-log path is not covered by it.
No snapshot is taken in the no-snapshot cases (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 10m), which is normal operation for clusters below the snapshot threshold.
excluded: Multi-node clusters and network partitions: the probe is a single-voter cluster, so the observed election abort is a progress loss and the vote-check consequence is source-read, not executed here.

basis.prefix: Fresh in-memory transport, InmemCommitTrackingStore log store, InmemStore stable store, InmemSnapshotStore; BootstrapCluster writes the single-voter configuration at index 1/term 1; first NewRaft elects the node as leader; five Apply commands are committed; optional user snapshot; Shutdown; second NewRaft on the same stores with a new transport sharing the same address. The harness never fabricates log entries or configuration state: all durable state comes from real bootstrap, real elections, real commits and a real snapshot.

comparisons.description: With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, the restarted node must still report the bootstrapped voter.
Control: the same restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the configuration, isolating the committed-prefix replay as the cause.

Control: with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a snapshot that carries the configuration, the restarted node keeps the configuration, showing that the loss is specific to configurations that only exist in the skipped committed log prefix.
